description:
Authoritative seven-PR split supplied by Jad:
PR1: Email and web bridge capabilities (user marked green/PR; no independent merge verification).
PR2: Shared capability-driven BO settings, TransportRequirements struct and shared resolver.
PR3: Support dark mode in channels.
PR4 (this epic/feat/delivery_plan): Outgoing attachment contract, lazy acquisition/materialization, validation, grouping and delivery plans.
PR5: Plan execution through Jido and email adapters, exact SMTP MIME sizing, failure policies, partial outcomes, confirmation and history.
PR6: attach_documents Action, authorization/provenance, opaque aliases, request-scoped stream selection and Agent executor propagation.
PR7: Workflow run_agent, notify_person and notification delivery integration.

Agreed PR4 contracts: Outgoing adds only attachments: []; no delivery wrapper, selection errors or plan. Plans remain internal to Channel. Consume current capability_snapshot/FileSettings/TransportRequirements.resolve contract; preserve optional unresolved limits, and never replace shared BO settings or add a bridge-owned requirements resolver. Metadata planning remains pure; acquisition primitives are lazy and reused by PR5. Existing materialization security is retained now; PR6 adds tool-level authorization/provenance.
Existing DeliveryConfirmation remains unchanged unless a strictly necessary PR4 contract adaptation is demonstrated; multi-receipt/history extensions belong to PR5.
No AttachDocuments, Agent selection accumulator or workflow/notification wiring in PR4. Closed .8/.10 mean removed from this PR, not implemented; PR6/PR7 will be planned separately.
Source ../zaq-feat-channel-files is reference only. No wholesale cherry-pick, application edits, commit/push or external publication authorized by planning.
Backend integration/property tests cover PR4; no new BO UI/browser E2E scope. Existing test behavior changes require explicit approval.
PR4 order: .1 -> .2 -> .3 -> .4 -> .9 -> .11. PR5 transport tasks .5/.6/.7 moved to zaq-9j8 and do not block PR4.
Action reuse: canonical Outgoing builder, current pure resolver/FileSettings and existing materialization boundary; planner/preparation are Channel-local implementation details, no new Action.

comments.text: Refined final execution order: .1 -> .2 -> .3 -> .4 -> .5 -> .6 -> .7 -> .8 (selection Action) -> zaq-6rc.10 (producers) -> .9 (integration review/docs) -> zaq-6rc.11 (post-review coverage/final validation). This supersedes the earlier shorter graph; still one linear DAG.

Execution authorized by current user request in feat/delivery_plan; planning-only wording and older PR5/6/7 sequencing are superseded. Baseline clean at 6d94a2813. Required order .1 -> .2 -> .3 -> .4 -> .9 -> .11; no commits, pushes, merges or dependency changes. Backend unit/integration/property scope; no browser E2E required. Existing test expectations will be retained.

Module-context evidence: A/mental model: Outgoing is the cross-role payload; Channels owns metadata decisions and transient content. B/responsibilities: builder propagates explicit Records/routing; Attachments validates/packs; Preparation acquires; existing Api/bridges deliver text; Materialization owns redemption security. C/dependencies: pure supplied requirements; DecodeBase64 via Jido.Exec; Materialization/TrustedContext; injected local router/config. D/contracts: supplied pipeline result -> Outgoing; Outgoing + resolved requirements -> separate plan/error; explicit Record + trusted context -> transient bytes/error. E/state: no new process, database, cache, temporary-file or global state; immutable source/plan, caller-owned acquisition lifetime. F/traces: result -> builder -> existing dispatch/formatter/bridge/confirmation; resolver -> planner; explicit acquire -> signed handle verification -> registered materializer -> role event -> content validation. G/invariants: stable ordered indices, no incoming echo, no metadata acquisition, no nil-identity elevation, distinct known/NA/unknown limits. H/risks: size drift/encoded payload overhead and adapter declarations remain executor responsibilities; raw uploaded bytes cannot estimate publication encoding. I/tests: focused builder/grouping/property/real-handle security plus existing delivery/resolver/confirmation regressions. J/unknowns: exact provider request sizing and external file declaration releases intentionally belong to PR5. No ownership changes or new Actions.

PR4 implementation complete in requested order .1 -> .2 -> .3 -> .4 -> .9 -> .11; all six tasks closed with evidence. Outgoing carries only attachments; pure Channel-local plans and lazy secure acquisition/actual-content validators are implemented, with owning Channels docs and new focused tests. Existing text/API/confirmation behavior retained, no production attachment executor enabled. mix q PASS; fresh full coverage12448 PASS and97.2% overall, executable PR4 files100%; final mix precommit12448 PASS. No remaining implementation or validation blockers. Epic remains in_progress awaiting explicit final human approval required by docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md Phase6 and eventual authorized landing. User has prohibited commit/push/merge; HEAD stays6d94a2813. PR5/6/7 work remains excluded.

PR-review skill review of uncommitted PR4 at HEAD 6d94a2813 against fix/channel-dark-theme: request changes, two reproduced medium-severity inline findings. (1) lib/zaq/channels/delivery/preparation.ex:98 rejects encoding utf-8, although JidoConnectBridge.extract_downloaded_content/build_downloaded_record emit that for downloaded text and the existing list_files inline-content test preserves it. Preparation.acquire on a valid text Record with content hello/encoding utf-8 returns invalid_attachment_encoding. Accept established raw-text encoding and add producer-to-acquisition coverage. (2) lib/zaq/channels/delivery/attachments.ex:107 treats all Record.size values as raw lower bounds. EmailBridge.Attachment.to_record sets size from MIME encoded_size. Real to_record metadata for base64 aGVsbG8= has size 8; planner rejects at max_attachment_bytes 5 even though acquire with those content bytes returns size 5 successfully. Preserve size semantics; treat encoded-only source size as unknown raw size or use a justified lower bound, then check actual bytes after acquisition. Add real email Record planning coverage. Fresh review validation: all four new PR4 suites 38 PASS (3 properties), six existing builder/requirements/confirmation/materialization suites 75 PASS (4 properties), total 113. Inspected all 10 changed/untracked PR4 files, related Record/JidoConnect/email producers and materialization boundaries. No production/test edits, Git publication or posted PR comments. No GitHub PR exists for feat/delivery_plan yet.

Remediation authorized in existing dirty worktree; preserve all uncommitted PR4. New dependency order .12 -> .13 -> .14. Previous .9/.11 validation predates review findings and does not validate these fixes. No existing test expectation changes planned: add producer-backed regressions only. No E2E/UI scope. Source-size projection will recognize durable communication_media/email:imap metadata, including hydrated Records, without decoding content or changing Record.size; other base64 producers keep known raw sizes.

Review remediation complete: .12 accepts established raw utf-8 bytes unchanged; .13 preserves MIME encoded Record.size and treats durable IMAP-source raw size as unknown during planning, while retaining known raw-size behavior for other producers. Regression-first evidence recorded in each issue. .14 reviewed alternatives, completed fresh coverage12458 passing and final precommit202 passing; all changed PR4 executable production lines100% covered. No executor activation, sending, permission changes, dependency changes or existing test expectation changes. Existing uncommitted PR4 preserved; no commit/push/merge. Epic remains open for final human approval. Unknown raw sizes still require actual-byte validation by future executor, as designed.

No inline or general findings (0 high/medium/low). Full coverage and precommit were not rerun in this read-only review; latest successful implementation validation remains recorded in .14.
